title: Spanheim: Mary's honor is grateful thought, preaching of her virtues, and commendation of her glory
source_text: XXXVI. Sic Frederico Spanhemio Honor Beatae Virgini Mariae debitus (ex quo de honore Sanctis aliis convenienti judicium fieri potest) est primo cogitatio & commemoratio honorifica insignis illius honoris, quo Deus illam prae omnibus creaturis pro gratiosa sua bonitate dignatus fuit, ut mater illius & esset, & diceretur, qui omnium Pater est, & Dominus. Secundo praedicatio virtutum ejus, quae nobis in sacris litteris describuntur, pietatis, charitatis, humilitatis, constantiae, & aliarum id genus virtutum, quae singulariter in eximio hoc Dei organo eminuerunt, & omnibus in exemplum proponi debent. Tertio commendatio gloriae & beatitudinis qua fruitur in caelis. Dubiorum Evangelicorum part. 2. dub. 48. num. 4.
pass_a_gloss: Thus for Frederick Spanheim the honor owed to the Blessed Virgin Mary (from which a judgment can be made about the honor fitting the other Saints) is, first, an honoring thought and commemoration of that remarkable honor by which God, of his gracious goodness, deigned her above all creatures to be, and to be called, the mother of him who is the Father of all, and the Lord. Second, the preaching of her virtues which are described for us in the sacred letters: piety, charity, humility, constancy, and other virtues of that kind, which singularly stood out in this excellent instrument of God and ought to be set before all as an example. Third, the commendation of the glory and blessedness which she enjoys in heaven. Evangelical Doubts, part 2, doubt 48, number 4.
pass_b_english: Spanheim's account of the honor due to Mary is also the pattern for other Saints.
First comes honoring remembrance that God, in sheer goodness, made her the mother of the Lord who is Father of all.
Second, preaching the virtues Scripture records in her, as an example.
Third, commending the glory and blessedness she enjoys in heaven.
